notes.meaning: A father urges his student to hold fast to God's instruction and obey it from the inner heart, not just on the outside. God's truth brings a long, fruitful life and real peace, which means true well-being and satisfaction. Following God's law protects our health on earth and leads to eternal life with Him.

God's people are told to keep steady love and truth with them at all times, making these virtues a fixed part of their character. Tying them around the neck like a precious seal and writing them on the heart keeps them ready for every choice. When someone walks in kindness and honesty, both God and people notice, approve, and show them favor.

True wisdom begins by placing full reliance on the Lord rather than leaning on our own limited thinking, which easily breaks like a weak stick. In every daily choice, big or small, we must seek God's guidance and submit to His will. When we depend on Him, He promises to direct our steps and clear away hindrances to lead us safely home.

Thinking too highly of one's own cleverness ruins a relationship with God, so true wisdom means showing deep respect for Him and turning away from sin. Living a life of calm faith and self-control brings physical health and deep refreshment to the whole body. A quiet conscience before God strengthens a person from the inside out.

God calls His people to honor Him by giving the very first and best part of their income to His service, showing that everything they have belongs to Him. Giving generously to God and caring for the needy does not make a person poor, but invites God's blessing on what remains. When we honor God with our goods, He faithfully provides plenty for our needs.

When troubles and trials come, believers must not ignore them or lose heart under them. God's discipline is not punishment from an angry judge, but loving correction from a caring Father who wants His children to grow in wisdom and goodness. Hard times show that God treats us as His beloved children and is training us for our own good.

A person who searches for and finds godly wisdom discovers the greatest happiness possible. This wisdom is far more valuable than traded silver, solid gold, or rare jewels, because worldly wealth cannot save the soul or satisfy the heart. True spiritual understanding is a treasure worth giving up everything else to obtain.

Wisdom holds out the chief blessing of a long and fruitful life in her right hand, along with true riches and honor in her left. Walking in God's ways brings deep inner peace and clean joy that far exceeds any passing earthly pleasure. Holding onto wisdom restores the life that was lost in the Garden of Eden, serving as a tree of life that sustains the soul.

God did not create the universe by accident, but set the earth on a solid base and shaped the heavens through His perfect wisdom. By this same understanding, He controls the deep waters below the ground and causes the clouds to drop dew and rain upon the earth. Because creation itself is built on God's wisdom, those who live by it are guided by the very power that holds the world together.

Believers are warned never to look away from God's wisdom, but to keep good judgment and clear thinking guarded inside the heart. These virtues give spiritual energy to the soul when a person feels weak and drooping. They also adorn a person's life and speech like a beautiful chain of gold, earning genuine respect.

Living by God's wisdom keeps a traveler safe during the day, protecting both body and soul from stumbling into sin or sudden trouble. At night, a clean conscience and trust in God's watchful care drive away fears of darkness, danger, or harm. A believer can sleep peacefully, resting under the care of the Lord who never slumbers.

When sudden disasters strike or ruin crashes down upon evil people, the righteous have no need to panic. The Lord Himself is the solid ground of their confidence, watching over them even when judgment sweeps through a land. He promises to protect their feet so they are not trapped by danger or paralyzed by terror.

God expects His people to pay their just debts and share with those in need whenever they have the power to help. Refusing to give or telling a neighbor to come back tomorrow when the help is already on hand is selfish and wrong. Doing good promptly fulfills the law of love and shows that we are faithful caretakers of what God has lent us.

It is treacherous and wrong to secretly plot harm against a neighbor who lives nearby and trusts in your honesty. In the same way, people must avoid starting arguments, bringing baseless charges, or dragging others into legal fights when no wrong has been done. God calls His people to be quiet and peaceful neighbors who do not stir up strife.

People may feel tempted to envy violent men who gain power and wealth through unjust force, but they must never copy their ways. The Lord finds devious, crooked people disgusting, no matter how successful they appear in the eyes of the world. In contrast, God welcomes honest and upright people into His close friendship, sharing His covenant love and counsel with them.

Even if an evil person lives in a grand mansion, God's curse rests upon that household, bringing inner misery and eventual ruin. Meanwhile, the modest home of a godly family enjoys God's daily presence and blessing, which brings true peace. The real worth of a home depends on God's favor, not on its size or earthly riches.

God opposes proud people who scoff at religion and mock what is right, turning their own arrogance into public humiliation. On the other hand, He shows favor and gives gracious help to the humble who patiently submit to His will. True honor comes only through quiet humility before God.

Those who follow God's wisdom will receive lasting honor as their rightful family inheritance, shining in God's presence. Fools may chase earthly glory, but their foolish choices will ultimately lift them up to public disgrace and shame. A person's final end reveals whether they walked in God's wisdom or followed their own folly.
